problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization of a globally convex C³ function f:E→ℝ. A global minimizer x* exists with ‖x0−x*‖≤R and f(x0)−f(x*)≤Δ; no strong convexity is required.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/PointwiseHessianConvex.lean: spec.admissible, ContDiff, ConvexOn, and minimizer existence clauses.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: Oracle 0 returns ∇f(x) exactly at every queried point, independently of history and oracle seed. Gradient calls have a separate fixed budget. No function-value oracle is supplied.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/PointwiseHessianConvex.lean: spec.numOracles, spec.Reply, and spec.admissible oracle-0 clause; LongTails/Template.lean: executeWithTrace and Convergence.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: Oracle 1 returns the full exact Hessian D(∇f)(x), represented as a continuous linear operator E→L[ℝ]E. Hessian calls have a separate fixed budget; no oracle noise or approximation is allowed.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/PointwiseHessianConvex.lean: spec.Reply and spec.admissible oracle-1 clause; LongTails/Template.lean: executeWithTrace.

distinctive_assumptions.label: generalized_smoothness
distinctive_assumptions.details: The pointwise operator-norm bound ‖D²(∇f)(x)‖≤M₀+M₁‖∇f(x)‖ holds globally, with M₀,M₁≥0. This bounds the third derivative and does not assert a two-point Hessian inequality with the same constants.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, with its induced norm; the setup imposes no dimension-dependent restriction.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Public information includes x0, M₀, M₁, R>0, Δ>0, and ε>0. The initialization bound ‖D(∇f)(x0)‖≤H₀ has H₀≥0 hidden from the algorithm, although the supplied oracle budgets depend on H₀.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/PointwiseHessianConvex.lean: Public, Params.H₀, spec.publicInput, spec.valid, and spec.admissible initial-Hessian clause; LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence.makeAlgorithm.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The output is a point in E satisfying f(output)−f(x*)≤ε for a global minimizer x*.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: The objective-gap guarantee holds almost surely under the joint algorithm-seed and oracle-seed distribution. The setup permits randomized algorithms.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/PointwiseHessianConvex.lean: spec.successful almost-everywhere clause; LongTails/Template.lean: Algorithm.law and Convergence joint product measure.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The formulation uses gradient-dependent pointwise third-derivative control and a hidden initial-Hessian bound, together with separately budgeted exact gradient and Hessian oracles.

descriptionHtml:
Convex Minimization with Hessian Access

We consider minimizing a three-times continuously differentiable convex function f:E→R on a finite-dimensional real inner product space E. We assume a gradient-dependent third-derivative bound, a hidden bound on the Hessian at a given starting point x0∈E, and bounds on its distance and objective gap to a global minimizer x⋆∈E. Two exact oracles return ∇f(x) and ∇2f(x) at x∈E, respectively. For a tolerance ε>0, the goal is an output x¯∈E satisfying f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤ε almost surely under P, the law of the algorithm’s randomness.

The optimization problem is minx∈Ef(x). The norm ∥⋅∥ is induced by the inner product on E, and ∥⋅∥op denotes the induced operator and multilinear norms. We regard ∇2f(x) as a linear operator from E to E and ∇3f(x) as a trilinear form on E. The parameters satisfy M0,M1,H0≥0,R,Δ,ε>0. The algorithm receives E, x0, M0, M1, R, Δ, and ε; the hidden parameter H0 may enter only the oracle-call budget.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Regularity and convexity). The function f belongs to C3(E;R) and, for every x,y∈E and t∈[0,1], f((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)f(x)+tf(y).

Assumption 2 (Third-derivative bound). For every x∈E, ∥∇3f(x)∥op≤M0+M1∥∇f(x)∥.

Assumption 3 (Initial Hessian and minimizer bounds). At the given starting point, ∥∇2f(x0)∥op≤H0. There exists x⋆∈E such that f(x⋆)≤f(x)for every x∈E,∥x0−x⋆∥≤R,f(x0)−f(x⋆)≤Δ.

Queries to either oracle may be made at any point of E. Gradient calls and Hessian calls are counted separately. After the allotted calls, the output must satisfy f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤εP-a.s.

Convex f∈C3(E) on a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, with ∥D3f(x)∥≤M0+M1∥∇f(x)∥ everywhere. An attained minimizer x⋆ satisfies ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R and f(x0)−f(x⋆)≤Δ; ∥∇2f(x0)∥≤H0. Here M0,M1,H0≥0 and R,Δ,ε>0. Exact gradient and Hessian access; target f(xout)−f(x⋆)≤ε for every seed.

import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.ContDiff.Defs
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Function
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.FiniteDimension

namespace LongTails.Setups.PointwiseHessianConvex

open OracleTemplate MeasureTheory

structure Public where
  E : Type
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [innerE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [finiteE : FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  x0 : E
  M₀ : ℝ
  M₁ : ℝ
  R : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ

attribute [instance] Public.normedE Public.innerE Public.finiteE

structure Params extends Public where
  H₀ : ℝ

abbrev spec : Setup where
  numOracles := 2
  Params := Params
  Public := Public
  Instance p := p.E → ℝ
  Query p := p.E
  Reply p := p.E ⊕ (p.E →L[ℝ] p.E)
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput := Params.toPublic
  valid p := 0 ≤ p.M₀ ∧ 0 ≤ p.M₁ ∧ 0 < p.R ∧ 0 < p.Δ ∧ 0 ≤ p.H₀ ∧ 0 < p.ε
  admissible p f O :=
    ContDiff ℝ 3 f ∧
    ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ f ∧
    (∀ x, ‖fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ (gradient f)) x‖ ≤ p.M₀ + p.M₁ * ‖gradient f x‖) ∧
    ‖fderiv ℝ (gradient f) p.x0‖ ≤ p.H₀ ∧
    (∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧ ‖p.x0 - xstar‖ ≤ p.R ∧
      f p.x0 - f xstar ≤ p.Δ) ∧
    (∀ k x seed, O.answer k (0, x) seed = Sum.inl (gradient f x)) ∧
    (∀ k x seed, O.answer k (1, x) seed = Sum.inr (fderiv ℝ (gradient f) x))
  successful p f output P :=
    ∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧
      ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure _), f (output ω) - f xstar ≤ p.ε

end LongTails.Setups.PointwiseHessianConvex
